To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal allocation of a budget for riparian buffer land acquisition is not uniform across the entire watershed and that the optimal allocation depends on the value of the land.

(1) Riparian land acquisition is a binary optimization problem; (2) Riparian land can be ranked by its potential to contribute to water quality and wildlife habitat goals; and (3) A model that ranks land by its potential to improve water quality and wildlife habitats can be used to identify the land that should be acquired for riparian buffers.

1) the optimal size of a riparian buffer depends on the land use in the watershed, 2) the optimal size increases as the amount of nonpoint source pollution increases, and 3) the optimal size is greater for a lake than for a stream.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal allocation of a conservation budget among land parcels to maximize the benefits of a riparian buffer.
the problem of how to optimally allocate a limited budget to purchase land for riparian buffers in heterogeneous landscapes to maximize the benefits of water quality protection.
the optimal placement of a riparian buffer to minimize the cost of acquiring the land for the buffer while simultaneously maximizing the benefit to water quality.

the riparian buffer is a valuable tool in water conservation.
the riparian buffer is an important tool for water quality management, but that its effectiveness depends on the specific hydrologic and land use conditions of the watershed.
the use of riparian buffers to protect water is a very important conservation tool of the government and non-governmental agencies.

riparian buffer optimization models can help conservation agencies to maximize the benefits from their scarce funds by targeting the most effective areas for land acquisition.
